summary: NCCL stall suspected in multi-GPU (TP) replica — possible collective mismatch / stream ordering issue
description:
Issue summary
Acme AI is seeing intermittent request hangs/timeouts on their Dedicated cluster when running multi-GPU tensor-parallel replicas (A100 80GB, TP=4). During the affected windows, we captured NCCL debug output indicating a suspected collective mismatch / out-of-order collective sequence across ranks. Symptoms align with “silent stall” scenarios: GPU utilization drops to near-idle on one or more ranks, in-flight requests stop making progress, and the API layer eventually returns timeouts.

Customer impact
- Streaming chat requests hang (no tokens emitted) and then time out.
- p99 latency spikes + elevated 504s from gateway for the affected route.
- Incident-level impact during peak hours; Acme AI has implemented a temporary concurrency cap but is still seeing sporadic stalls under burst.

Environment
- Deployment: Dedicated (customer VPC peering)
- Region: us-east
- Hardware: A100 80GB (4 GPUs per replica)
- Runtime version: 1.18.6-redwood (customer pinned), canary candidate 1.19.0-rc2 available
- Models: llama-70b-instruct (TP=4), mixtral-8x7b-instruct (TP=2)
- Workload pattern: mixed prompt lengths (2k–16k), streaming enabled, bursty concurrency (spikes), cancellations observed (client disconnects)

What we collected
1) NCCL debug logs (sanitized) from an affected replica (rank 0 and rank 3). These were captured during a canary debug window (see INT-2219). Notable lines below.
2) Runtime structured logs showing TP step progress halting on a collective boundary.
3) Request IDs and approximate timestamps to correlate with tracing.

NCCL debug excerpts (sanitized)
Timestamp window: 2025-02-20 18:31:02–18:33:10 UTC

Rank 0:
- "NCCL INFO Launch mode: Group"
- "NCCL INFO comm 0x7f2a... rank 0 nranks 4 cudaDev 0 busId 0000:2b:00.0"
- "NCCL INFO Ring 00 : 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 0"
- "NCCL INFO AllReduce: opCount 184467 count 2097152 datatype 7 op 0 root -1"
- "NCCL WARN [Service thread] Connection closed by peer"
- "NCCL INFO Abort COMPLETE"

Rank 3:
- "NCCL INFO comm 0x7f93... rank 3 nranks 4 cudaDev 3 busId 0000:b1:00.0"
- "NCCL INFO AllReduce: opCount 184466 count 2097152 datatype 7 op 0 root -1"
- "NCCL INFO AllGather: opCount 184467 count 524288 datatype 7"
- (No further progress; no matching AllGather on rank 0 at same opCount)

Interpretation (tentative)
- Rank 3 appears to advance to a different collective (AllGather) while rank 0 is still at AllReduce for the same opCount+1 boundary. This is consistent with a collective ordering divergence between ranks (could be stream/event ordering, conditional path in kernel code, cancellation/early-exit path, or scheduler starvation causing one rank to enter a different phase).
- The “Connection closed by peer” and abort is likely a downstream symptom once one rank times out/aborts; we need to determine the first divergence trigger.

Current hypothesis (needs Eng confirmation)
- Ordering/synchronization issue around NCCL collectives on separate CUDA streams when mixed prefill/decode interleaving occurs, potentially amplified by request cancellation and/or CUDA graph capture constraints.
- Alternate hypothesis: scheduler fairness/starvation causes one rank to delay a collective while others advance, leading to mismatch.

Asks / next steps
- Eng Kernels (Hiro/Grace/Yuki): validate whether current TP implementation can hit divergent collective ordering under mixed workloads and where stream/event sync is missing.
- Eng Scheduling (Sofia/Julian/Lena): evaluate starvation risk in prefill-heavy batches preventing collective alignment.
- SRE (Rafael/Aisha): confirm alerting signals available for “heartbeat gaps per rank” and whether this was visible during incident windows.

Temporary mitigations (currently applied / recommended)
- Apply concurrency cap per replica (Acme currently set to 24; previously 48).
- Disable CUDA graph capture on TP routes (if enabled) for stability testing.
- Prefer Dedicated-first canary on runtime 1.19 with NCCL stream/event sync hardening + stall detectors once available.

References
- Slack incident thread: #incidents (1740165551-sev1-dedicated-timeouts-suspected-tp-hang)
- Slack runtime thread: #eng-runtime (1739812205-nccl-collective-ordering-suspected-mismatch)
- In-flight fixes: PR-21853 (stream/event sync hardening), PR-21841 (scheduler guardrail), PR-21912 (error surfacing), PR-21860 (watchdog/drain)

Attachments
- Redacted NCCL log bundle uploaded to support case (internal link): support-attachments/SUP-48377/nccl-debug-logs-2025-02-20.tgz
- Correlation sheet (request ids + timestamps): support-attachments/SUP-48377/request-correlation.csv

Initial read suggests collective mismatch: rank 3 advances to AllGather while rank 0 still on AllReduce (opCount skew). Looping in runtime kernels + scheduling. Linked to INC-2025-02-17-DEDICATED-TP-HANG and related tickets SUP-48321/SUP-48344.

2025-02-20 19:25 UTC — Liam O'Rourke (TAM/CS liaison): Confirmed with Acme: workload is bursty, streaming enabled, and they do see client disconnects at peak (front-end retries). They can keep concurrency cap at 24 for 48 hours, but want an ETA for a stability build. Requested we provide a recommended set of env flags (NCCL debug, async error handling) that won’t materially degrade throughput.

2025-02-20 20:10 UTC — Rafael Mendes (SRE): We can enable extra NCCL/runtime debug logging for a bounded canary window (1–2h) but want a rollback plan + confirmation it won’t emit sensitive payloads. Please track under INT-2219. Also: during the Feb 17 window, GPU metrics showed one rank dropping to ~0% SM while others stayed moderate, consistent with a stall at a sync boundary.

2025-02-20 21:03 UTC — Grace Kim (Kernel Eng): The opCount skew is suspicious. Two common paths: (1) missing stream sync before ncclGroupEnd when upstream work is on another stream, (2) conditional collective in code (e.g., different branch taken) caused by early-exit/cancellation. Can you confirm whether these logs correspond to a period with client cancellations? If yes, please correlate request ids around 18:31–18:33 UTC.

2025-02-21 00:18 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support): Correlated timestamps: there were 17 client disconnects (HTTP/2 stream resets) in the 2-minute window prior to the first observed stall. Also saw a spike in "request_cancelled" events on the same route. Added correlation CSV to attachments. This aligns with cancellation path possibly leaving ranks out of sync.

2025-02-21 09:40 UTC — Hiro Tanaka (Mgr Kernels): Acknowledged. We have a hardening PR in flight around stream/event sync at NCCL boundaries (PR-21853) and a separate cancellation deadlock fix (PR-21890). For this ticket, we need to verify whether cancellation can cause ranks to skip a collective (mismatch) vs just hang waiting. We’ll run the benchmark-lab repro with induced cancels once Rina posts the harness config.

2025-02-24 16:12 UTC — Yuki Sato (Kernel Eng): Early repro in lab: with mixed prefill/decode + forced cancellations at ~1–2% rate, saw a stall once in ~90 minutes on A100 TP=4. Not yet a clean deterministic repro, but traces show a stream wait preceding the NCCL call on rank 0. This points toward missing event sync (matches PR-21853 intent).

2025-02-26 18:55 UTC — Aisha Bello (SRE): Draft alerting plan: heartbeat gap per rank + in-flight collective counters. Once PR-21834 and dashboard panels merge, we can page on “heartbeat gap > 30s” correlated with request timeout rate. For Acme, we’ll route alerts to SRE oncall + tag runtime oncall. Added notes to incident follow-ups.

2025-03-03 10:22 UTC — Liam O'Rourke (TAM/CS liaison): Shared interim guidance with Acme: keep concurrency cap at 24; disable CUDA graphs for TP routes; schedule a 1.19 canary once approved. Acme agreed to provide another 24h window for debug logs during canary if needed, but prefers a “fix-first” approach rather than more logging.
